findings.action: R2/D1 unmet: the ready check parses text whose terminated HTML comments were already removed (line 454), so a comment in the accepted limits section, inline code included, passes with spec.ready=true while the sealing reader refuses the whole section; accepted_limits.go:210 drops the problems, so the bundle seals no limit and nothing says so.

R2 bypass: a comment on or before the section heading line (trailing, leading or multi-line) makes commentInAcceptedLimitsSection skip the heading, so comments in the section go undetected, are stripped, and a cut limit is sealed with no problem; with an unterminated one the problem is returned but the cut limit is still returned and sealed.
R2 bypass: the comment detector treats a heading indented under a limit as ending the section (the parser does not, since R1), so a later limit L2 holding a comment is returned for sealing cut.

D1 violated: the detector ignores code fences and tracks only the first comment of a line, so a fenced example section outside the real one (with a comment in or after it), or a commented example opened after another comment on the same line, refuses the real section and discards its limits.

R1 is partial: when the limit marker is itself indented, a heading-like line indented one to three spaces but not deeper than the marker still ends the section, and the limit is sealed cut with no problem.

The backtick parity rule misreads Markdown: an unterminated comment after a stray backtick is no longer reported (the earlier first-comment check reported it), and a marker in a double-backtick code span is reported as an unterminated comment.

The new ninth --finding field is stored for any disposition, and a non-approving manual attestation skips the sealed-limit check (review_bundle.go:3167), so it can record an unsealed limit such as L9; R4 closes only the draft path.
The R6 test calls renderWithinLimitFindings directly; removing its calls at review_closeout.go:104 and :328 would not fail it, so the review-check and closeout-check output is untested.

The changed derivation also applies when runConclusionDiffers recomputes older records: a run-backed non-approving attestation an earlier engine recorded within an unsealed limit would now differ from its draft. No affected record was demonstrated in this repository.
